## Purpose
Settings → Cleanup. It deletes what the project has accumulated, one area at a time or all of it ("Complete cleanup", back to a fresh install with the seeds restored). It also clears "This browser's data". Every run needs the confirmation phrase.

## Responsibilities
- Server: `settingsApi.cleanupPreview` gives per-target counts; `cleanup` runs with the chosen targets and the phrase "DELETE" (`ConfirmDialog`).
- Rows and results: `TargetRow`, `ResultCard`.
- Browser: `clearBrowserData` / `browserItemCount` clear chat sessions, planner history and other localStorage items, then reload. The results survive in sessionStorage (`readStoredResult` / `writeStoredResult`).

## Key elements
`CleanupPanel`.

## Control flow
React rendering; data through React Query hooks where noted.

## Data, state and side effects
localStorage and sessionStorage.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- Backend `/api/settings/cleanup` (`app/cleanup`). The vault target needs the vault admin token.

## Error handling and edge cases
None noted.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **The page reloads after a browser cleanup,** because in-memory stores would write their data straight back.
- **Nearly every page's data changes after a cleanup,** so all queries are invalidated.

## How to rebuild this file
Implement as described; copying the file is the reliable route for exact styling.
